subject: Dedicated capacity: pricing concession & throughput SLOs (Nimbus Health)
messages:
From: Alex Patterson <alex.patterson@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask + throughput guarantees

Rishi —

Thanks again for the demo this week. Nimbus is ready to move from PoC to production but we need a commercial that matches the economics we were offered elsewhere and stronger throughput guarantees. High level:
- Target workload: ~1200 qps-equivalent inference tokens/day across three services; peak concurrency suggests a dedicated pool equivalent to ~8 H100 GPUs (we can share across models).
- Required SLO: 95th pct latency under our production rps profile, with clear fallback if capacity is constrained.
- Contract preference: 12–18 month reserved commit; looking for pricing parity with their offer (they quoted a 30% unit discount vs public list + onboarding credits).

Can Redwood match or come within 5% on price? We value Redwood's runtime and controls but need price competitiveness plus a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration. If you can provide a firm committed throughput and a small credit we can fast-track procurement.

Happy to hop on a call today.

—Alex
Alex Patterson
Head of Platform Engineering, Nimbus Health
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Patterson <alex.patterson@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + throughput guarantees

Alex —

Appreciate the clarity and congrats on the move to production. We can structure a Dedicated reservation that gives predictable throughput and the operational controls you outlined. Quick thoughts:
- Proposed footprint: 8-GPU pool (H100-equivalent) reserved for a 12-month commit.
- Throughput guarantee: committed baseline with a soft burst pool and automated fallback to a compatible model variant if capacity is constrained. We can SLO the p95 latency for your primary model class; I will confirm exact ms after we run the throughput estimate.
- Commercial: standard reserved pricing + we can offer a 15% committed discount and a $25k onboarding credit today.

I understand the competing quote at ~30% + credit. That is out of our standard approval band, so I need an exec/finance exception to go deeper. If you can give me a short term window (48–72 hours) I will escalate for approval and come back with a final counter. Would 25–30% plus a $40–50k credit land you? If so, I can ask for an exception today.

Attaching our initial throughput estimate and a clean commercial term sheet so procurement can review while I work approvals.

Best,
Rishi
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: FWD: Nimbus Health — request for 30% discount + $50k credit (exec approval request)

Team —

Nimbus is pushing a competitive match: they have a 30% committed discount + $50k onboarding credit on the table if we don't move quickly.

Commercial asks (summary):
- 12-month reserved commit for an 8-GPU H100-equivalent pool
- 30% off our public reserved rates (they claim competing vendor gave this)
- $50k one-time onboarding credit for migration and initial burst costs
- Requesting firm p95 latency SLO and written fallback behavior

Why this matters: Nimbus is a high-profile healthcare customer (large wallet, potential reference and marketplace channel), and they will likely expand to dedicated capacity across other teams if we win. We can trade a deeper discount for a locked 12-mo commit and a minimum monthly usage floor.

Ask: can we approve up to 30% discount + $50k credit? If not, what ceiling do we have — and any other guardrails (minimum monthly commit, clawbacks, limited-term credit) to reduce risk? I attached: throughput_estimate.xlsx, commercial_terms_redline.pdf, NIMBUS_MSA_redlines.pdf.

I need a yes/no or counter by EOD today to keep momentum.

Thanks —Rishi
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FWD: Nimbus Health — request for 30% discount + $50k credit (exec approval request)

Rishi —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. Nimbus is strategic; this looks like a classic win-to-scale motion. I am willing to grant an exception with the following commercial guardrails:

1) Approve a 25% discount off reserved pricing (not the full 30%).
2) Approve a one-time onboarding credit of $40,000.
3) Contract must be 12-month minimum with a monthly minimum spend floor equal to 70% of the committed monthly ramp. If Nimbus fails to hit the floor, we claw back credits pro rata.
4) Legal (Laura) to sign off on the MSA redlines — no changes to our liability caps or data residency commitments.
5) Throughput SLO: we will commit to p95 latency targets for the agreed primary model class; any SLA credits will be limited and capped. Operations to publish a clear fallback policy (model variant fallback + cross-region burst) — Rishi, please coordinate with Infra.

Reasons: we buy down the price enough to be competitive, keep financial protections in place, and limit operational exposure via clear fallback and caps. If Nimbus accepts these terms, we should fast-track a Term Sheet and DocuSign routing.

Marissa
VP, Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Patterson <alex.patterson@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@nimbushealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: pricing concession & throughput SLOs (Nimbus Health)

Alex / Dana —

Good news: we can do an approved concession to get you live quickly. Final commercial summary (subject to legal redlines):
- Reserved: 12-month committed pool, 8 H100-equivalent GPUs
- Price: 25% discount off our reserved list rate
- One-time onboarding credit: $40,000 applied to month 1 invoice
- Monthly minimum: 70% of committed spend; failure to meet floor triggers pro rata recovery of credits over remaining term
- SLOs: we will commit to p95 latency for the agreed model class; SLA credits capped per the Terms. Operations will publish fallback behavior (model variant fallback + cross-region burst) in the term sheet.

I attached a redlined commercial term sheet for quick review (commercial_terms_redline.pdf). When you're ready I will route the Term Sheet + MSA to DocuSign: https://docusign.net/prepare?env=prod&doc=ABCD1234. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876543.

If you accept, we can kick off onboarding as early as Apr 12 assuming signatures and payment clearance. Please confirm and I will send the DocuSign packet.

Thanks — looking forward to getting Nimbus live.

Best,
Rishi
From: Alex Patterson <alex.patterson@nimbushealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dana Ortiz <dana.ortiz@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: pricing concession & throughput SLOs (Nimbus Health)

Rishi —

Thanks — we can accept the 25% + $40k credit with the 12-month commit and minimum floor. Before DocuSign we have two small asks: 1) confirm the p95 target number (ms) for the primary model we tested, and 2) include the fallback behavior in the term sheet language (we need written assurance of cross-region burst + model-variant fallback order).

If you can add those two specifics to the redline, we will sign the DocuSign packet tomorrow and aim for the Apr 12 start date.

—Alex
